subject: general
question: P and Q together can fill a cistern with water in 8 hours. If P alone can fill the cistern with water in 16 hours, then in how many hours will Q alone fill one-fourth of the same cistern with water?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM of 8 and 16 = 16 units.

Combined efficiency of P and Q = 16 ÷ 8 = 2 units/hour.

Efficiency of P = 16 ÷ 16 = 1 unit/hour.

Efficiency of Q = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour.

Time for Q to fill 1/4th of the cistern = (16 × 1/4) ÷ 1 = 4 ÷ 1 = 4 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P and Q together to fill the cistern = 8 hours

Time taken by P alone to fill the cistern = 16 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given hours

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Q = Efficiency of (P + Q) − Efficiency of P

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Total work required by Q = 1/4 of the total cistern capacity

⇒ Required Work = 1/4 × 16 = 4 units

⇒ Time taken by Q alone = Required Work ÷ Efficiency of Q

⇒ Time taken by Q alone = 4 ÷ 1 = 4 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns vs Time & Work

It operates on the exact same logic as regular Time & Work problems. A filling pipe adds positive work, while an emptying pipe or a leak contributes negative work.

Work & Efficiency Relation

Time taken is inversely proportional to efficiency. Therefore, the ratio of time taken by two working entities is exactly the reciprocal of their efficiency ratio.

Partial Work Execution

When asked to calculate time for a fraction of the work, always calculate the complete work (LCM) first, find the required fraction of units, and then divide it by the specific efficiency of the respective person or pipe.
